meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided to give Owen a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. What else do you have besides the checker?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in. And your own procedure says you look at his other work, so where is it?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, Hale. One file history is not a case. What else?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Maybe he got the scene wrong. Is it anywhere in the play?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
A wrong quotation is not a confession. Whatever comes next, nothing goes on his record, and his class hears nothing.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and a final draft. And you still haven't told me what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, in writing, tonight, with the date set before December 1. Owen will do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. And the zero comes out of the gradebook the day the new mark goes in.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. I'll confirm with him tonight. Put the room and the supervisor's name in your email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed under procedure 4.4 to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday, November 12, not in front of his class, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require the room and the supervisor's name in writing, and the zero removed from the gradebook the day the new mark is entered. I expect your written confirmation tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, and she still wants the terms in writing tonight with the room and supervisor named and the zero cleared when the new mark goes in, which is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: you let her search the play herself for the line the essay quoted, which mattered because it was something she could check with her own eyes rather than take on your word.
What cost ground: nothing; you owned the early zero in one sentence and never accused Owen, though you left her point about the outline unanswered.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed on a late night in October, October 28 just before midnight, close in kind to what she saw though not the same moment; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said students change their minds between an outline and a final draft, answer it before moving to the offer, for example by pointing out that the version history shows no in-between draft where that change could have happened.
